coverage.note: All 6 first-party files covered by all 3 tools, but ONLY after working around default test-exclusion in each tool. See toolInvocations.

findings.description: safeTransferFrom(from, address(this), stableAmount) pulls the stablecoin from an arbitrary `from`. The function spends only the ANTIMATTER allowance (_spendAllowance(from, msg.sender, amount) at line 214); the stablecoin leg relies solely on `from`'s ERC20 approval to this contract. A caller holding an antimatter allowance can therefore also cause `from`'s separately-approved stablecoin to be pulled. Needs manual adjudication of whether the two-allowance coupling is intended.
findings.note: Slither impact=High confidence=High. Do NOT auto-suppress; the allowance-coupling question is the substantive one for Tier 2.

findings.description: State written after external call: setPhUSD reads minter.phUSD() then assigns phUSD (lines 127-128); setPhUSDMinter reads newMinter.phUSD() then assigns phUSDMinter (lines 140-141). Both are onlyOwner and the external callee is the owner-supplied minter/token, so exploitability is bounded by Law 3 (non-malicious owner).
findings.note: Aderyn ranks High. Likely down-ranks to Low/QA; passing through at potential-medium for dedup, not asserting High.

findings.description: stableAmount = amount / scale (255) then stableAmount * scale != amount (256). The multiply-after-divide is the deliberate exactness check that reverts with AmountNotRepresentable rather than silently truncating. Probable false positive.
findings.note: Detector fires on an intentional round-trip guard.

findings.description: Strict equality `mintedForStable == 0` used as a post-mint receipt guard (reverts PhUSDNotReceived). Strictness is the point of the guard; probable false positive, but a partial-mint that yields a non-zero-but-short amount would pass this check.
findings.note: The residual question for Tier 2 is under-mint, not zero-mint.

findings.description: Tuple destructuring of minter.stablecoinConfigs(stable) discards 5 of 7 fields. Intentional; flagged only because dropped fields could matter if the minter's config semantics change.

Local variable `decimals` shadows the inherited ERC20.decimals() / IERC20Metadata.decimals() function. Readability hazard: within toStableAmount, `decimals` is the STABLECOIN's decimals, not this token's.

rescueERC20 declares `onlyOwner nonReentrant`; nonReentrant is not the first modifier, so the ownership check runs outside the reentrancy guard. Low impact here (onlyOwner is a pure view check) but it is the documented anti-pattern.
Owner-privileged surface: contract is Ownable (21) with onlyOwner on setPhUSD (124), setPhUSDMinter (136), setApprovedMinter (151), rescueERC20 (263).
findings.note: Law 3: report only as centralization inventory. Malicious-owner vectors are NOT to be filed. Retained so Tier 2 can test for non-obvious FOOTGUNS (e.g. repointing phUSDMinter under live approvals).

findings.description: Modifier onlyApprovedMinters is invoked exactly once. Worth confirming the approved-minter set is actually load-bearing on every path it should gate (i.e. that no mint entry point is missing the modifier).
findings.note: Reframed as a coverage question rather than a style nit.

findings.description: Magic literals 18 / 10 in the decimal-rescaling math (lines 252, 254).
findings.note: Style; 18-decimal assumption is documented in NatSpec.

findings.description: Return value of antimatter.transfer(stranger, 4e18) is ignored in a test. Corroborated by Aderyn unsafe-erc20-operation and unchecked-return at the same line.
findings.note: Test-harness code, not production. Low value.

findings.description: approve()/ERC20 return values ignored at Annihilation.t.sol lines 62, 133, 155, 285. Corroborated by Aderyn at the identical lines.
Address state variables set without zero-address checks (lines 16-17) in the ReentrantStable mock.
findings.note: Mock/attacker-harness contract; a missing check here is intentional test surface, not a defect.
